search_cards.name: search_cards

parameters.description: Optional. Text to look for, matched without regard to case across the card's name, description and both meanings. To find one card by name, use 'Get a tarot card' instead.
parameters.name: query

parameters.description: Optional. Only return cards of this suit. Coins, disks, staves, rods, batons, chalices and blades are accepted as other names for the same four suits.
parameters.name: suit

parameters.description: Optional. Only return cards carrying this number. A suit runs 1 (Ace) to 14 (King), with 11 to 14 being the Page, Knight, Queen and King; the trumps run 0 to 21.
parameters.name: value

parameters.description: Optional. Narrow to the 22 trumps or the 56 suit cards.
parameters.name: arcana

parameters.description: Optional. Return at most this many cards. Left blank, every card that matched comes back. The API sends its whole answer at once, so this shortens the result rather than saving a request, and 'total matched' still reports the full count.
parameters.name: limit

arcana.description: The arcana that was filtered on, or null.

items.description: One tarot card, with its meanings and its description.

arcana.description: Which arcana the card belongs to: 'major' for one of the 22 trumps, 'minor' for one of the 56 suit cards.

court_rank.description: The rank of a court card: 'page', 'knight', 'queen' or 'king'. Null for every other card.

desc.description: Waite's description of the card's picture, exactly as the API sends it. 'description' is the same text under a clearer name.

description.description: Waite's description of what is drawn on the card, which is what to show someone who is looking at the image.

is_court_card.description: True for a Page, Knight, Queen or King. The 16 court cards are the ones usually read as people.

is_major_arcana.description: True for one of the 22 trumps. Branch on this rather than comparing the arcana string.

meaning_rev.description: The reversed divinatory meaning, exactly as the API sends it. 'meaning_reversed' is the same text under a clearer name.

meaning_reversed.description: What the card means when it comes out reversed, in the same words. Reading reversals is optional: many readers work upright only, which is what turning off 'Allow reversed cards' does.

meaning_up.description: The upright divinatory meaning, exactly as the API sends it. 'meaning_upright' is the same text under a clearer name.

meaning_upright.description: What the card means when it comes out upright, in A. E. Waite's words from 'The Pictorial Key to the Tarot' (1910).

name.description: The card's name, e.g. 'The Fool' or 'Ace of Cups'. This is what 'Get a tarot card' takes and what a reading prints.

name_short.description: The card's short name, e.g. 'ar00' for The Fool. Stable, and the only identifier the API has, so it is what to match on rather than the display name.

reversed_keywords.description: The reversed meaning split the same way.

suit.description: The suit the card belongs to: 'wands', 'cups', 'swords' or 'pentacles'. Null for a trump, which belongs to no suit.

type.description: The API's own word for which arcana the card belongs to, 'major' or 'minor'. Kept as the service sends it; 'arcana' is the same value under the word a reader uses.

upright_keywords.description: The upright meaning split into the separate terms Waite wrote it as, e.g. ['Folly', 'mania', 'extravagance']. A meaning written as a sentence comes back as a single item.

value.description: What the card's number is called, e.g. 'ace', 'four' or 'queen'. A trump carries its number here instead.

value_int.description: The same number as an integer, so it can be compared or sorted. A suit runs 1 (Ace) to 14 (King); the trumps run 0 (The Fool) to 21 (The World).

count.description: How many cards came back in this result.

first.description: The first matching card, lifted out of the list. Null when nothing matched.

arcana.description: Which arcana the card belongs to: 'major' for one of the 22 trumps, 'minor' for one of the 56 suit cards.

court_rank.description: The rank of a court card: 'page', 'knight', 'queen' or 'king'. Null for every other card.

desc.description: Waite's description of the card's picture, exactly as the API sends it. 'description' is the same text under a clearer name.

has_cards.description: True when anything matched. Branch on this rather than on the list being empty.

names.description: Just the card names, for a message or a check that does not need the whole record.

query.description: The text that was searched for, or null.

suit.description: The suit that was filtered on, after any other name for it was translated. Null when no suit was set.

total_matched.description: How many cards the API matched, from the 'nhits' it reports. The API has no paging, so this is the whole match rather than one page of it, and it differs from 'count' only when a limit here cut the list short.

truncated.description: True when a limit cut the list short, so 'total matched' is larger than 'count'.

description: Read tarot cards from Tarot API, the free reference for the 78 cards of the Rider-Waite-Smith deck. Draw a card of the day, deal a whole spread with every card in its position and the reading written out ready for a model to interpret, or look one card up by name and get both of its meanings. Browse the deck by suit, by court rank, by number or by a search across every card's description and meanings. Card names, descriptions and divinatory meanings come from A. E. Waite's 'The Pictorial Key to the Tarot' (1910), the companion to the deck most modern decks are based on. No account or API key required.
